title: How to Grill Sliced Figs with Honey on a Non-Stick Mat
meta_description: Master the art of grilling sliced figs with honey using a BBQ grill mat. Learn prep tips, flavor combos, and how to keep delicate figs from sticking or flare‑up
html:
Why Grilling Figs on a BBQ Mat Is a Game‑Changer

When you think of figs, you picture a sweet, almost caramel‑like fruit. Slicing them and searing the flesh on a grill gives them a smoky depth that pairs perfectly with a drizzle of honey. The trick? Using a BBQ Grill Mat so the delicate fruit doesn’t stick or tear. These reusable, non‑stick mats keep flare‑ups at bay and let you cook figs on any grill—gas, charcoal, or electric—without the fuss.

Preparing the Figs: A Quick Checklist

Start with fresh, ripe figs. Look for plump, slightly soft skins with a deep, glossy color. Avoid bruised or overly soft ones, as they’ll fall apart on the grill.

  1. Wash figs gently under cold water, pat dry.
  2. Slice each fig in half, cutting through the core. The halves should be about 1/2‑inch thick.
  3. If you prefer a slightly crisp edge, lightly brush the cut side with a little olive oil.

Set aside a small bowl of honey. A light drizzle after grilling amplifies the fruit’s natural sweetness and creates a glossy finish.

Setting Up Your BBQ Grill Mat

Place the BBQ Grill Mat on your preheated grill. The mat should be at a moderate heat—high enough to sear the figs but low enough to avoid burning the honey or the fruit’s flesh. A good rule of thumb is to aim for 350°F (175°C). If you’re using a charcoal grill, spread the coals evenly and let them settle before laying the mat.

Because the mat is non‑stick, you don’t need to oil it. This keeps flare‑ups minimal and the cleanup a breeze. Just make sure the mat is clean before each use; a quick wipe with a damp cloth removes any residue.

Grilling the Figs: Step‑by‑Step

Place the fig halves cut side down on the mat. Let them sear for 2–3 minutes until you see nice grill marks and the skin begins to blister slightly. Flip the halves over and grill the cut side for another 1–2 minutes. The goal is a warm, caramelized interior with a lightly charred exterior—no burning.

Once the figs are grilled, remove them from the mat and immediately drizzle honey over the cut side. The residual heat will melt the honey into a sweet glaze that coats the fruit. If you like a bit of crunch, sprinkle a pinch of sea salt or a few crushed pistachios on top.

Serving Ideas to Elevate Your Grilled Figs

Grilled figs are versatile. Pair them with:

  • Fresh goat cheese and arugula on a toasted baguette.
  • Crumbled feta and a drizzle of balsamic reduction over a bed of spinach.
  • Chopped nuts and a splash of lemon zest for a Mediterranean twist.
  • A scoop of vanilla gelato for a sweet dessert.

For a quick snack, serve the figs on a plate with a dollop of ricotta and a sprinkle of cinnamon.

Why a BBQ Grill Mat Makes All the Difference

Grilling delicate foods like figs on a standard grill can be tricky. The fruit’s thin skin often sticks, and the high heat can cause flare‑ups that burn the honey or create uneven cooking. The BBQ Grill Mat solves both problems: its non‑stick surface keeps the figs intact, and its heat‑resistant design prevents flare‑ups by keeping fat and juices away from the flame.

After cooking, the mat is dishwasher safe, so you can reuse it over and over. That’s a win for both convenience and sustainability.

Tips for the Perfect Grilled Fig

  • Use a lighter honey (such as wildflower or orange blossom) to add a subtle flavor twist.
  • For an extra smoky note, add a pinch of smoked sea salt after drizzling honey.
  • If you’re grilling multiple figs, keep them covered with a clean cloth to maintain heat and prevent drying out.
  • Experiment with different fruit sizes; smaller slices cook faster and give a more intense caramelization.

FAQ

Can I use the BBQ Grill Mat on a charcoal grill?

Yes! The mat is heat‑resistant and designed for all grill types. Just make sure the coals are evenly distributed and the grill is preheated.

How do I clean the BBQ Grill Mat after use?

Wipe it with a damp cloth or rinse under warm water. It’s dishwasher safe, so you can also toss it in the dishwasher for a deeper clean.

What if the figs are too soft and might tear on the grill?

Choose firmer figs or slice them a bit thicker. If they still tear, lightly dust the cut side with flour or cornstarch to help hold them together.
